mission_reference: Earlier SLS Block 1 / Artemis I-era reference values
thrust_reference_condition: NASA published nominal/max reference values; source-specific rating level applies

mission_reference: Earlier SLS Block 1 / general booster reference; see Artemis II-specific row for launch vs maximum thrust
thrust_reference_condition: Older NASA summary lists approx 3.6 million lbf per booster without explicitly labelling sea-level/vacuum; kept unclassified in this legacy record.
reported_mass_basis: NASA SLS reference guide: approx 1.6 million lb each (loaded) and 219,000 lb empty; direct conversions. Empty value is source-described empty booster mass.
data_status: Published dimensions, thrust, burn duration and loaded/empty mass descriptors; propellant mass not separately asserted here
notes: Earlier row retains source-described loaded/empty mass values. More recent Artemis II reference-guide thrust ratings are stored in a separate mission-specific record; do not combine rows as if one exact flight configuration.

stage_name: Interim Cryogenic Propulsion Stage (Artemis I reference)
thrust_reference_condition: NASA reported nominal thrust; do not relabel as vacuum unless source explicitly states it
reported_mass_basis: Approximate fully fueled ICPS mass as stated in NASA reference guide; not a dry mass
data_status: Artemis I variant-specific reference only; do not assume identical ICPS engine variant across later missions
notes: Variant-specific Artemis I ICPS: NASA identifies RL10B-2. Do not assume this engine variant for Artemis II; see S31 and separate Artemis II row.

mission_reference: Artemis II SLS Reference Guide (October 2025 prelaunch estimate)
thrust_reference_condition: NASA Artemis II guide: approx 418,000 lbf per engine at launch and up to 512,300 lbf at 109% power; retained as at-launch/max rather than conflated with sea-level/vacuum labels
reported_mass_basis: RS-25 engine mass per engine from NASA Artemis II guide (7,750 lb / 3.52 metric tonnes each); does not represent total core-stage dry mass.
data_status: NASA-published Artemis II prelaunch reference estimate; not actual launch telemetry or a complete stage mass statement
notes: NASA guide gives approx 2.2 million lb total LOX/LH2 and about 480 s core-stage operation. Do not combine this mission-specific propellant figure with the earlier Artemis I-era 987.5 t / 85.3 t row without recording the different source revision. NASA guide also lists each RS-25 engine at approx 3.52 t; recorded as individual engine mass in reported_component_total_mass_kg.

mission_reference: Artemis II SLS Reference Guide (October 2025 prelaunch estimate)
thrust_reference_condition: NASA Artemis II guide: approx 3.3 million lbf at launch and approx 3.6 million lbf maximum per booster; source labels as launch/max thrust, not sea-level/vacuum pair
reported_mass_basis: Per booster: approx 1.6 million lb loaded and 219,000 lb empty in NASA guide. Propellant mass shown is derived by subtracting the two rounded published mass values; it is not a separately quoted exact propellant load.
data_status: Published Artemis II prelaunch estimates; mass subtraction is derived/approximate
notes: Each booster burn duration approx 126 s. Do not present the derived propellant mass as a directly measured or exact manufacturer value.

mission_reference: Artemis II SLS Reference Guide (October 2025) plus NASA RL10 Fact Sheet (December 2025)
stage_name: Interim Cryogenic Propulsion Stage (Artemis II reference)
thrust_reference_condition: NASA RL10 fact sheet published thrust value; retained as nominal/other because this row does not normalize the condition label across engine ratings
reported_mass_basis: NASA Artemis II guide gives approx 32,748 kg fueled and 3,719 kg unfueled; propellant mass 29,029 kg is derived by subtraction and is approximate.
data_status: Artemis II-specific reference; total/unfueled masses are approximate and propellant mass is derived
notes: NASA RL10 fact sheet distinguishes RL10B-2 for Artemis I from RL10C-2 for Artemis II/III. Do not substitute the Artemis I engine variant.
